title: Internal Hom base change through a filtered finite-free coefficient colimit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with a sheaf of commutative rings $R$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], relative derived tensor computed using K-flat complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Assume filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of sheaves of commutative $R$-algebras, with each $S_i$ isomorphic as an $R$-module sheaf to $R^{d_i}$ for a finite nonnegative integer $d_i$. Let $S=\varinjlim_i S_i$ be its sheaf-algebra colimit, whose underlying module is the filtered sheaf-module colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $K\in D(R)$ satisfy the following continuity property: for every diagram $(M_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ of cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with a common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced map
$$\varinjlim_i H_R(K,M_i^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_R(K,\varinjlim_i M_i^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism, with filtered colimits computed by exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial representatives. For every $L\in D(R)$ with bounded-below cohomology, the canonical evaluation-transpose comparison
$$S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\longrightarrow H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. It is natural in $K,L$ and in compatible morphisms of the algebra diagrams. Its restriction to $D(R)$, under the evaluation-normalized scalar-adjunction identification, is the composite
$$\begin{aligned}
S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)&\simeq\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes_R H_R(K,L))\\
&\simeq\varinjlim_i H_R(K,S_i\otimes_R L)\\
&\simeq H_R(K,S\otimes_R L).
\end{aligned}$$
In this formula a bounded-below representative of $L$ is used, and the stage comparisons are the evaluation-defined ones. They are compatible with every transition map of the diagram, independently of choices of finite bases. No constructibility of $L$ or finite Tor amplitude of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work with the universally quantified strict representatives P and bounded-below L, the fixed functorial K-injective resolution I and its natural augmentation eta. Use the recorded strict Hom, degree-zero tensor and evaluation-normalized comparison models. No new choice of representatives or derived tensor-Hom adjunction is needed.

Use the stated strict scalar-Hom identification lemma. Its extension functor equals the given E by Functor.ext, using the pinned object and map functions. Its sigma formula agrees with ScalarNormalized: a scalar multiple of the generator at 1 is the generator at that scalar, by linearity of the sheafification unit. Its sigma_formula and sigma_unique therefore prove existence and uniqueness of the public scalar comparison, whose definition is unchanged.

Apply the finite-free stage theorem and filtered continuity theorem to the underlying coefficient diagram. Exact filtered colimits preserve the stage quasi-isomorphisms. Colimit extensionality and comparison naturality give the two strict cocone squares. Two-out-of-three proves that the comparison at the colimit is a quasi-isomorphism. This is the existing proof of filteredColimit_comparison; it does not require continuity at the possibly unbounded resolved complex.

The canonical single-complex total-tensor comparison gives a natural isomorphism from tensor(T,-) to the termwise tensorLeft T functor. Compose it with nu from the strict scalar-Hom identification. The canonical comparison takes tensorGenerator to the ordinary sheafification-unit pure tensor; nu_pure then gives the stated extensionGenerator formula. All constructions and their section normalizations are those of the existing declarations.

Use theta and theta_evaluate from the stated strict scalar-Hom identification. Its local evaluation is definitionally the recorded homValue, and its extension section is the given extensionGenerator. Thus theta is exactly the chain-Hom isomorphism required here, with its full evaluation formula; no duplicate chain-Hom construction is made.

Precompose the asserted restriction square with the invertible nu.hom on the source, so that nu followed by its inverse cancels. Evaluate on tensorGenerator(s,f), then on x, using the representative interface extensionality theorem. Apply the generator formulas for nu and theta, ScalarNormalized and Normalized. Both evaluations agree by the naturality square for the R-resolution augmentation applied to nu followed by the restricted S-resolution augmentation. This proves equality of chain maps before localization.

Tensoring with a finite product of the tensor unit is exact, including the empty product. The filtered-continuity module proves that finite limits commute with the assumed exact filtered colimits and hence that tensoring with the colimit of this finite-free diagram preserves finite limits. Reuse those general exactness lemmas and tensor-colimit preservation. Transfer left exactness along the ordinary tensor identification E followed by U. Restriction is exact and conservative, so E preserves finite limits; its left adjoint property gives finite colimits. Thus E preserves homology. By the exact left-adjoint/right-adjoint lemma, U preserves K-injective complexes. The existing functorial-resolution API supplies K-injectivity, quasi-isomorphic augmentations and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms by resolved Hom. Apply independent-universe Hom invariance to raw Hom between K-injective targets.

Transport the quasi-isomorphism in step 3 along the recorded coefficient-colimit isomorphism. In the restriction square of step 6, nu and theta are isomorphisms. The remaining comparison augmentation maps are quasi-isomorphisms: restriction carries the resolved S-complex to a K-injective R-complex, and step 7 applies Hom invariance to its R-resolution augmentation. The other side is a composite of quasi-isomorphisms. Cancel these factors by two-out-of-three and use exact conservative restriction to reflect quasi-isomorphisms. This proves the scalar numerator is a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness of E and resolved Hom invariance prove the denominator is a quasi-isomorphism too.

Localization inverts the scalar numerator and denominator; the fixed coefficient-Hom resolution factorization is already an isomorphism. Their specified composite is derivedComparison, so it is invertible. The normalized scalar comparison equals the strict-model sigma by sigma_unique, and sigma_natural proves its two-input naturality. Coefficient-diagram naturality is the existing comparison naturality applied to the actual colimit map. All public statements, definitions and the unit route are unchanged.

lean.note: Universal representative formulation: P is any K-flat representative of K, L any strictly bounded-below representative of the second derived input, and E the ordinary scalar-extension functor with its specified objects and maps. Exact finite-free-colimit scalar extension computes its derived functor on these representatives. The actual map in D(S) is derivedComparison, fixed by pure-tensor evaluation and the actual localization factorization. Auxiliary declarations give its strict termwise-colimit formula, scalar-adjunction normalization and naturality. No mathematical hypothesis or clause of the node is changed. R6: the unchanged strict representative definitions are now attached to def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models and def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-roof in Sheaf.Paper.DerivedInternalHomFilteredColimitData; comparison_existsUnique is attached to lem-sfb-internal-hom-comparison-exists.
